title: Desktop Repository-Selection Git Process Storm and Runtime Amplification Audit

preflight.note: Opened immediately after an operator reproduced a host-impacting RepoPact Workbench repository-selection failure that spawned repeated visible Git child processes and could starve normal Windows process-management UI. WI055 remains immutable completed history; this item owns diagnosis, remediation, repository-wide amplification audit, and regression evidence.

acceptance_criteria.text: Add executable reproduction/instrumentation proving the current defect mechanism: native repository open/read paths must not spawn Git subprocesses proportional to work-item count or to the number of frontend read commands issued for one repository generation.

Inventory every production external-process launch site in Rust and Python plus every desktop polling/event/read fan-out that can reach them; classify each as repeated/high-frequency, bounded one-shot, intentional long-running, test-only, or separately owned security substrate, with no unreviewed process-launch site left at closeout.

Centralize Rust Git child-process execution used by repository/validation paths behind a testable helper; on Windows captured GUI-origin Git children use no-console creation flags, while stdout/stderr/status semantics remain portable and no shell wrapper is introduced.

Bound Rust Git child behavior: read-only metadata commands are non-interactive, have explicit finite timeout/termination behavior, and cannot create an unbounded process/thread storm when Git hangs, a refresh is repeated, or repository size/work-item count grows.

Compute repository Git topology facts needed for one snapshot/refresh at most once per refresh generation, including common-dir/worktree discovery and tracked-path facts needed by validation; per-work-item files_under, contract discovery, dashboard rendering, or record enumeration must not independently rerun identical Git topology queries.

Refactor repository indexing so repeated traversal of work-item directories reuses the already computed topology/exclusion set and preserves WI053 linked-worktree, ignored-directory, deterministic-order, and record-relative-reference semantics exactly.

Make validate_snapshot consume the supplied immutable snapshot/index/topology rather than reopening and independently recrawling the repository; validation, dashboard projection, graph, analysis, and native read views for one generation derive from the same canonical repository facts.

Audit RepoPactCore and other reusable Rust call sites for repeated snapshot construction; preserve explicit fresh-snapshot APIs where semantically required but ensure multi-view/high-frequency consumers have a generation/session API that does not accidentally recrawl on every read.

Cache the current immutable repository snapshot/generation in the native desktop session and serve overview/work/decision/evidence/graph/analysis/validation reads from it; initial open, explicit refresh, accepted watcher refresh, and successful mutation/post-apply refresh are the operations that replace the cached generation.

Repository selection may perform bounded initial indexing/validation, but subsequent frontend overview/work/decision/evidence bootstrap calls and tab reads must not trigger independent filesystem/Git recrawls; parallel frontend reads over one generation are projections of cached native state.

Watcher refresh is single-flight and coalesced: one burst produces at most one refresh computation at a time, unchanged canonical snapshot tokens do not emit duplicate semantic refresh events, and self-originated/apply events cannot feed an unbounded refresh loop.

Watcher-specific generated-directory filtering covers native build/output churn relevant to desktop host safety, including .git, target, node_modules, .venv, Python caches, build/dist and other demonstrated generated paths, without silently broadening canonical governance-ignore semantics unless parity evidence justifies it.

Do not hold the global desktop state mutex across avoidable long-running filesystem traversal, validation, or Git child-process waits; refresh publication remains generation-safe and stale computations cannot overwrite a newly selected repository.

Add host-safety regression coverage with realistic many-work-item repositories proving Git invocation count is bounded by a small constant independent of item count, parallel native read fan-out performs no new Git work for an unchanged generation, and watcher bursts remain bounded.

Add static/regression enforcement preventing raw production Rust Git process launches from reappearing outside the approved process helper and preventing desktop/Tauri/frontend code from acquiring generic shell/process authority.

Review non-WI050 Python user-facing Git/tool subprocess helpers for the same containment class; safe bounded query helpers receive explicit timeout/non-interactive behavior where appropriate, intentionally long-running build/launcher operations are documented rather than given unsafe blanket timeouts, and repeated-loop process spawning is either removed or explicitly bounded.

WI050 admission/guard/platform/service process-launch sites are audited for amplification/timeout risk but not silently changed under WI057; any material security-substrate defect is recorded against WI050 with exact evidence and ownership before WI057 closes.

Run a native Windows reproduction only after safeguards exist: select the RepoPact repository and a second scratch/adopted repository, demonstrate responsive navigation/refresh/switch behavior, record Git process invocation/concurrency evidence, and confirm no visible terminal storm or host starvation occurs.

Preserve WI053-WI055 semantics and the WI056 design baseline: Python suite, Rust workspace tests, 20/20 conformance, WI050 8/8 corpus, linked-worktree/reference parity, desktop frontend/type/security/build checks, frozen-surface integrity, and no WI050 authority migration remain green.

Closeout evidence records the operator-observed failure, confirmed root causes, complete process-launch classification, pre/post Git invocation and concurrency behavior, Windows child-process configuration, snapshot/topology/cache lifecycle, watcher convergence, Python process-safety disposition, native reproduction result, regressions, residual risks, and an explicit determination that WI056 may resume.
